extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO search and examination staff and patent applicants filing under the Harare Protocol (including PCT applicants interacting with ARIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and quality requirements for conducting patent searches and preparing ARIPO search reports (and related communications) under the Harare Protocol and relevant WIPO standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful search — discretionary factual determination
rubrics_metrics.description: What is or is not 'meaningful' is a question of fact for the Search and Examination Section to determine. The exercise of the Search Examiner's discretion will depend upon the facts of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'meaningful' should be construed reasonably: not every difficult search is 'not meaningful', but a search may be regarded as not meaningful if it would serve no useful purpose or the results would be meaningless (for example, due to Harare Protocol non-compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims lacking support / insufficient disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad or speculative claims supported only by a limited disclosure may render a meaningful search over the whole claim impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases a meaningful search could be performed only on the narrower, disclosed invention (e.g., specific examples). A complete search may be de facto impossible or of no useful purpose if the claim's breadth makes it indefensible in subsequent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims lacking conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim set with so many claims or possibilities that it is unduly burdensome to determine the matter for which protection is sought can render a complete search impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where lack of conciseness makes the search de facto impossible or the claim set indefensible, the search may be restricted or not carried out in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims lacking clarity (parameters preventing comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant defines the invention by parameters that prevent meaningful comparison with prior art (e.g., prior art uses different or no parameter), clarity is lacking and a meaningful search may be impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search may be restricted to worked examples or to how the desired parameter is obtained; the basic principle is clarity and openness about what has and has not been searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to indicate subject-matter for search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office considers it impossible to carry out a meaningful search of all or some claimed subject-matter, it will invite the applicant to file, within two months, a statement indicating the subject-matter to be searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation will give reasons and may indicate the claimed subject-matter on which the Search Section considers a meaningful search feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant reply to invitation — indication or argument
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant replies indicating subject-matter and a meaningful search on that basis is possible, the Office will search that subject-matter; if the applicant argues why a full search is possible and the Examiner is convinced, a full search will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely reply, the Examiner determines what to search. If the applicant indicates subject-matter still not fully searchable, the Examiner will determine the subject-matter to search consistent with the response, or may declare no meaningful search possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: More than one independent claim per category — invitation to indicate which to search
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims as filed do not comply with Administrative Instruction 21, the Office will invite the applicant to indicate, within two months, claims complying with Administrative Instruction 21 on the basis of which the search is to be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used where multiple independent claims in the same category exceed permitted numbers or exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply regarding multiple independent claims — selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant indicates a particular independent claim to be searched, the Office will conduct the search on that claim; if no timely indication is provided, the first claim in each category is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may indicate more than one independent claim where exceptions apply; if the Office finds indicated claims do not fall within exceptions, only the independent claim with the lowest number indicated will be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of extended ARIPO search report / search opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The search opinion will invite the applicant to limit the application to claims which have been searched and will explain reasons if the Examiner disagrees with the applicant's arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the applicant disputes a finding and the Examiner is not convinced, reasons will be indicated in the search opinion and consequences in examination will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where claim fees are not paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim has been deemed abandoned due to non-payment of claims fees, the applicant cannot indicate it for search and it will not be searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will search the first independent claim in the category for which claims fees have been paid; if all independent claims are abandoned, no invitation will be sent and none will be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications lacking unity — procedure and partial search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application lacks unity of invention, the Office may raise the unity issue and invite the applicant to indicate independent claims to be searched; it may also apply procedures for additional search fees for other inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lack of unity is apparent when inviting, Office will identify the first invention and invite indication for that invention; a partial search report will be prepared on the invention first mentioned, and applicant may be invited to pay additional search fees for other inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims in restricted searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims depending directly or indirectly on an independent claim excluded from the search are likewise excluded from the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a dependent claim relies on more than one previous claim, only those dependencies that stem from searched claims will be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and minimum composition of search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic part of the search documentation consists of a collection of patent documents systematically accessible for searching; periodicals and other technical literature are also made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The systematically accessible part includes the minimum documentation required for an International Searching Authority under Rules 34 and 36.1(ii) PCT and extends somewhat beyond these minimum requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic access systems and search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must have computer facilities allowing use of the IPC (with finer internal subdivisions) and other classification systems and/or word searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches can be performed using IPC subdivisions, other classification systems or keyword/word searches as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT minimum documentation inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The systematically accessible search documentation includes the national patent documents that form the PCT minimum documentation as specified in Rule 34.1(b)(i) and (c) PCT (lists of countries and document types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific lists (e.g., certain national patent publications since 1920), published international and regional patent applications, and appropriate abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished patent applications excluded from search citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the search report do not include unpublished patent applications; completion of search for conflicting unpublished applications is entrusted to the Substantive Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only published documents can be cited in the search report prepared by the Search Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family system and representative document display
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office should keep a patent family system and typically display only one representative family member on-screen, with links to other family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all family members need be included in manual search files, but links and annexes should identify family members for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of search reports ARIPO will draw up
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO Office will draw up: (i) ARIPO search reports; (ii) supplementary ARIPO search reports concerning PCT applications; (iii) international-type search reports; (iv) search reports on behalf of national offices; and (v) search reports further to special work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In examination, additional search accounts may be drawn up when necessary and not published; this chapter sets out requirements for type (i) reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and mandatory contents of the standard search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard search report contains a main page recording important features: (i) the application number; (ii) the classification of the application; (iii) the fields searched; (iv) the relevant documents revealed by the search; and (v) the name of the examiner who executed the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search report or the declaration replacing it should be drawn up in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the patent application and type marking
rubrics_metrics.description: On the main page and supplemental sheets, the application is identified by its filing number and the type of search report is indicated (A1/A2/A3/A4 per WIPO ST.16 depending on publication/search timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct ST.16 marking: A1 for joint publication, A2 if application published before search, A3 for subsequent search report, A4 for supplementary ARIPO search report for international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of technology searched — IPC symbols listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not required by the Harare Protocol, the search report includes areas of technology searched as a list of IPC symbols up to the sub-class level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search is based on a previous search for a cognate subject, the sections consulted for the previous search are also identified by IPC symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of cited documents — bibliographic elements per WIPO standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents cited in the search report must be identified unambiguously by indicating the necessary bibliographic elements and comply with WIPO Standard ST.14, ST.3 and ST.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations are permissible only in special cases where strict adherence would require considerable extra cost and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling corresponding documents (family members and abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing 'corresponding' documents (family members or abstracts), the examiner need not cite all family members; one or more may be mentioned and family members are indicated using the '&' sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for citing abstracts instead of original documents include availability issues or language; when an abstract is cited, the original document must be input after the '&' sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language choice for cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When family members have equal technical content and are published before earliest priority, the examiner should choose which family member to cite by virtue of language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer documents published in an ARIPO language where relevance is otherwise equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary ARIPO search report with no documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances a supplementary ARIPO search report may list no cited documents and show 'No further relevant documents disclosed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the search opinion (if applicable) will give an opinion on patentability over the state of the art cited in the International Search Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of documents (X, Y, A, O, P, T, E, D, L) and their meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited are indicated by category letters: X (alone prejudices novelty/ inventive step), Y (relevant in combination), A (state of the art non-prejudicial), O (non-written disclosures) with accompanying relevance symbol, P (intermediate documents) with accompanying symbol, T (theory/principle), E (potentially conflicting patent documents with earlier filing/priority dates), D (documents cited in the application), L (documents cited for other reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinations of categories are possible; brief reasons should be given for 'L' documents; primary documents explicitly referring to others should be indicated appropriately (primary as 'X').

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between documents and claims (claim linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document cited should be accompanied by an indication of the claims to which it relates unless the document is category 'L'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same document may be indicated by different categories with respect to different claims. Each independent claim should be mentioned in the search report at least once with respect to at least one document published before the earliest priority date unless that independent claim is excluded from the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication and dates on the search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the search report was drawn up (the drafting date by the examiner) must be indicated, and the name of the examiner must appear on the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies to be attached to the search report — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report sent to the applicant and transmitted to Search and Examination must be accompanied by copies of all documents cited, except those appearing after the '&' symbol which are not designated for copying and communication to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cited documents are used to assess patentability in the search opinion and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic version of documents cited
rubrics_metrics.description: If parts of a patent document are published only by electronic means, an electronic version of at least those parts not available in paper form must be made available to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the whole document either as a combination of paper and electronic forms or in electronic form only so the applicant receives the complete document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family members and the '&' sign (copying rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally only a copy of the family member actually cited is supplied; other members are mentioned in an annex, but one or more further family members may be mentioned after the '&' sign and designated for copying and forwarding to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents after '&' designated to be copied will be included in the examination file and may be referred to in the search opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews or books — copies required
rubrics_metrics.description: When a cited document is a review or book, copies should be made of the title page and the relevant pages of the publication concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries, extracts or abstracts — forwarding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a cited document is a summary, extract or abstract published separately, a copy of that summary/extract/abstract is forwarded with the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Examiner considers the entire document is required, the full document must be cited and a copy attached. For online search results where original print is unavailable, a database print-out may be added in lieu of the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of search report and search opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO Office forwards the search report, the search opinion (if applicable), and copies of all cited documents to the applicant, including those after the '&' sign that have been designated to be copied and sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain an abstract whose purpose is to give brief technical information about the disclosure in the description, claims and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner determines the definitive content; the abstract is for technical information only and must not be used to interpret the scope of protection sought. It should be drafted as an efficient instrument for searching in the technical field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive content and examiner's role for the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is initially supplied by the applicant but the examiner determines its definitive content, normally published with the application; if the search report is published later, the abstract may be that resulting from examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider the abstract in relation to the application as filed and concentrate on conciseness and clarity without embellishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must: (i) indicate the title of the invention; (ii) indicate the technical field; (iii) contain a concise summary of the disclosure allowing clear understanding of the technical problem, gist of the solution and principal use (and chemical formula if applicable); (iv) not contain statements on alleged merits or speculative application; (v) preferably not exceed 150 words; (vi) be accompanied by indication(s) of figure(s) which illustrate main features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection accompanying the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should consider which drawing figure(s) to publish with the abstract and may alter text or select different figures if they better characterize the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may prevent publication of any drawing with the abstract if none are useful. Focus on conciseness and clarity and avoid altering merely to embellish the language.
